answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making identity expensive to forge and cheap to verify: each agent must lock a stake and build a record of attested work before its votes count, so a flood of fresh sockpuppets is like trying to cross a canyon with no bridge — possible only by paying the full construction cost for every crossing. Honest agents tend their reputation like a garden over time, compounding trust, while an attacker must fund each fake from scratch, so faking a majority costs more than any gain from gaming one round.
